newsitem.title: USA: Photran sees losses for next few months.
newsitem.headline: Photran sees losses for next few months.

text.p: Photran Corp said Monday it expects to continue to record losses for the next few months before productivity initiatives and the start-up of a second production line begin generating net income in the latter half of 1997.
Earlier, Photran reported a loss of $5.28 million or $1.25 a share for 1996, which included restated results for the first, second and third quarters.
"Management has three priorities: increase production, boost productivity and generate a sustainable profit," Paul Fink, chief financial officer, said in a statement.
"Our balance sheet is sound, our business prospects are strong and we're taking the right actions to make Photran a focused, efficient and profitable enterprise," he added.
In March, Photran laid off 21 full-time employees, or roughly 20 percent of its work force. The layoffs primarily affected positions in engineering, machining and research.
The company said it also terminated its lease on a 15,800-square-foot buliding that housed most of these employees.

Photran said it created an executive committee consisting of the vice president for finance and administration, the vice president for manufacturing and the vice president for technology. The company also hired a corporate controller.

In addition, it increased production of TN grade ITO-coated glass on its P-1 manufacturing line by almost 100 percent since the beginning of March 1997. In addition, it expects to begin production on the P-2 line in the second quarter. It expects to sell this line to Wintek Corp, its largest customer, for $2.9 million.
Photran added it is actively exploring market opportunities in Europe and the United States.
